correctness.rationale: Completing the Bargmann Gaussian integral gives Bf(z)=e^(mu1 z^2)G(z^2), G(w)=A+B exp(alpha w)+C exp(beta w), A,B,C>0, 0<alpha<beta; G(0)>0 excludes branched zeros. G=Gprime=0 forces B exp(alpha w)=-A beta/(beta-alpha), C exp(beta w)=A alpha/(beta-alpha). The magnitudes require equal explicit log-real coordinates, and phases alpha Im w odd pi, beta Im w even pi yield reduced alpha/beta=p/q with p odd q even. At each solution Gsecond=A alpha beta !=0, so exactly double. The zeros are w_j=xstar+pi i q(2j+1)/beta and z=+-sqrt(w_j). An exponential-Chebyshev three-function argument principle gives strip count beta T/pi+O(1) with multiplicity; bounded horizontal real strip transports count to disks, and w=z^2 yields weighted planar 2beta R^2/pi+O(1). Subtract the double-zero progression (beta/(pi q))*R^2 before lifting for distinct count 2beta(1-1/q)R^2/pi+O(1). Independent high-precision direct exponential tests on 14 double zeros at p/q=1/2 and 1/4 confirmed simultaneous G,Gprime=0 and Gsecond nonzero. Finite checks do not prove the bounded counting remainder.
